summary: The root فُلَانٌ (fulān) refers to "such a one" or "so-and-so," used as a placeholder for a person's name, typically male. فُلَانَةٌ (fulānah) is its female equivalent.
lane: فُلَانٌ ذ is a substitute for the proper name of a human being, (S, Msb, * K, TA,) i. e. of a male; (S, TA;) and in like manner , (Msb, K, TA,) for that of a female; (TA,) each without ال ; (Msb:) [the former may be rendered Such a one, or Such a man; and the latter, Such a woman: ] and الفُلَانُ and for other than a human being, (S, K, TA,) i. e. for a [particular] camel, (Lth, TA,) or for a [particular] beast, as in the saying, رَكِبْتُ الفُلَانَ [ I rode such a beast, i. e. such a male beast ], and حَلَبْتُ [ I milked such a beast ]: (Msb, TA:) فُلَانٌ has no dual nor pl.: (IB, TA:) [but] sometimes one says to a single person, mase., يَا فُلُ ; and to two, يَا فُلَانِ ; and to a pl. number, يَافُلُونَ : and in the fem., يَا فُلَةُ ; &c.; (K: [see more in art. فل :]) accord. to Kh, فُلَانٌ is of the measure فُعَالٌ ; and its dim. is : (TA:) or, as some say, it is of the measure فُلَانٌ , [originally فُلْوَانٌ ,] with و rejected, therefore its dim. is [originally فُلَيْوَانٌ ]; (T, L, TA;) like as إنْسَانٌ is [said by some to be] إنْسِيَانٌ , of which the ى is rejected. and therefore its dim. is أُنيْسِيَانٌ . (T, L.)

headwords.def: فُلَانِىٌّ the rel. n. of فُلَانٌ : it is rendered indeterminate by the affix ى ; and by means of the article اَلْ , it becomes determinate; therefore you say فُلَانٌ الفُلَانِىُّ [meaning Such a one, the person named in relation to such a one ], (TA,)
